summary: SSE stream becomes silent mid-generation after client backpressure and batch reshuffle
description:
Issue summary: Several NovaHealth customers report that SSE (server-sent events) chat responses become silent partway through long generations (typically 1200-2500 tokens). The TCP connection remains open, no FIN is observed, and the client does not receive final chunks or the terminating [DONE] event. This appears to have started after rolling autoscaler/worker tweaks deployed 2026-03-09.

Impact: Multiple customer sessions interrupted mid-response causing downstream application failures (form saves missing AI completion). Affected customers are on Dedicated capacity; estimated 12% of long-running chat requests in prod-us-west during the observed window. Customer visible symptom: streaming stalls (no data) for >60s and client eventually times out.

Environment: prod-us-west, dedicated cluster "nova-dc-03", streaming over SSE via edge-proxy -> streaming-gateway -> serving-runtime. Autoscaler policy recently adjusted to be more aggressive on quantized-worker eviction under memory pressure.

Initial hypothesis: Client-side backpressure (slow ACKs / small receive window) leads gateway to buffer; scheduler’s dynamic batching attempts to reshuffle inflight requests to maintain GPU packing, triggering a preemption or worker swap for a quantized fallback worker. During the swap the SSE stream experiences a short stall; combined with HTTP proxy coalescing and the client TCP stack, the stall crosses the client-side timeout and no graceful retry path is taken (no [DONE]).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use a long prompt that produces ~1500-2200 tokens on redwood-alpha-3b.
2) Establish SSE stream against prod-us-west endpoint routed to dedicated NovaHealth capacity (token from customer account).
3) Introduce artificial client-side receive slowness (tc qdisc netem delay 200ms + limit socket recv buffer to 8KB) to simulate backpressure.
4) Observe streaming output: initial tokens arrive, then a prolonged silence (>30s) before client-side timeout/abort. Capture tcpdump on client and gateway if possible.
5) Repeat while reproducer load causes scheduler to perform batch reshuffle (use load generator to produce concurrent short and long requests).
observed_behavior: Stream delivers initial token chunks, then becomes silent for an extended period without a connection close; server logs show the worker marked as preempted and a fallback worker spun up but no final flush event recorded to the SSE connection. Client eventually reports timeout and marks conversation incomplete.
expected_behavior: Worker preemption or fallback should gracefully forward remaining tokens (or emit an explicit abort/DONE event) so client can surface a deterministic error/retry. Streaming should not be silent mid-generation for healthy connections.
logs: [serving-runtime] 2026-03-10T09:14:28Z WARN worker=quant-q4 evicting worker due to memory_pressure=true preemptible=true
[customer-tcpdump] client shows continuous TCP window and no FIN; application-level last chunk received at 09:14:29Z
investigation_notes: Support triage: Collected customer request_id, procured pcap, verified client-side timeout set to 60s.
Reproduced in staging by throttling client recv buffer and running a mixed workload; observed similar silent window tied to scheduler reshuffle events.
Correlation seen between recent autoscaler policy commit (PR #6782) and increase in 'evict' logs in dedicated clusters during high memory pressure windows.

Hypothesis: aggressive eviction leads to worker preempt during in-flight streaming. The serving-runtime does not always flush KV/prefix buffers to the existing client connection during fallback; gateway/edge proxy coalescing may delay bytes until client-side buffer threshold, amplifying the stall.
Checked runtime metrics: spike in worker_preempt_count around 09:14, concurrent_kv_sync_latency increased from 30ms to 420ms during event window.

Reviewed gateway code path: fallback path writes directly to new worker stream but does not guarantee delivery if original stream writer has been paused by the scheduler (ticketed in code review notes).
Ran a controlled A/B in staging with autoscaler threshold relaxed: no stream silence observed under same simulated backpressure load.
Attached traces: link to flamegraphs and trace IDs included in GitHub PR comments.
comments: 2026-03-10 11:05 - Aisha Khan (Support): Customer provided request_id=abc123 and pcap. Reproduction attempts in staging succeeded with throttled client. Escalating to runtime team.

2026-03-10 13:22 - Marcus Li (SRE): Confirmed correlation with autoscaler commit. Pulling metrics for worker_preempt_count and kv_sync_latency. Assigning to serving-runtime squad for deeper code inspection.

2026-03-10 15:18 - Priya Shah (Runtime Eng): Found a code path where fallback_write does not set non-blocking flush when original writer is paused. Opening hotfix PR to ensure flush+ack behavior. See PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6782
2026-03-11 09:02 - Customer (NovaHealth): Customer notes this is high impact; they will temporarily increase client timeout to 120s as mitigation while fix is validated.

2026-03-12 07:40 - Marcus Li (SRE): Hotfix merged to staging, running soak tests with simulated backpressure. No silence observed in 12h soak. Planning prod rollout in maintenance window 2026-03-12 02:00-03:00 UTC.
root_cause: Aggressive autoscaler eviction policy caused quantized workers to be preempted during in-flight streaming. The serving-runtime fallback path failed to guarantee flush of remaining tokens to the original client connection when the writer was paused, and edge-proxy coalescing combined with client-side small receive window turned short stalls into full client timeouts.
resolution: Merged hotfix that: 1) ensures serving-runtime marks in-flight stream writers as non-blocking flushable during worker handovers; 2) adds a short 'graceful flush' period before worker eviction under streaming traffic; and 3) updated gateway to emit an explicit abort event if fallback cannot deliver within 5s. Deployed to prod-us-west 2026-03-12 02:15 UTC during maintenance window.
remediation: Back out aggressive autoscaler eviction thresholds for dedicated clusters until additional soak tests complete.
Add unit/integration tests simulating client backpressure and verify fallback flush semantics.
Update runbook: include guidance to raise client streaming timeout to 120s as a stopgap for customers on Dedicated when running long generations.
Monitor metrics: worker_preempt_count, kv_sync_latency, stream_silence_rate (new metric) across prod clusters.
Follow-up: investigate edge-proxy coalescing behavior under small receive windows to reduce burst coalescing for SSE connections.
